feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: shallow-to-moderate water tables (0.5-~40 m) are directly addressable with the ELM soil/aquifer column, but reaching 50 m and mechanistically tracking a pulse's arrival at the water table requires ELM-PFLOTRAN Richards-equation coupling.
answerable: Fraction of an infiltration pulse that recharges the water table (QCHARGE/QRECHARGE) as a function of initial water-table depth (WTD)
Time lag between the surface infiltration pulse and the recharge signal at the water table for each WTD
Attenuation/spreading of the wetting front through the vadose zone (H2OSOI, SOILLIQ profiles)
Water-table rise (ZWT change) per unit infiltration for shallow vs deep initial WTD
Partitioning of the pulse among storage change, drainage, and evapotranspiration
not_answerable: WTD deeper than ELM's discretized column (~42 m) without PFLOTRAN vertical grid extension
Lateral groundwater flow / regional aquifer connectivity (single-column has no lateral transport)
Fingered/preferential flow or macropore bypass (default Richards physics is homogeneous)
3-D water-table geometry or capillary fringe dynamics beyond 1-D column resolution

requires_capabilities: ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling for Richards-equation vadose-zone flow and vertical grid extension to 50 m
Idealized/synthetic DATM forcing to impose a controlled single infiltration pulse (e.g., 50 mm over 1 day) followed by a dry recession
Per-column initialization of water-table depth via finidat/cold-start override or PFLOTRAN initial pressure profile
Sub-daily history output to capture pulse arrival timing at depth
Single-point (single-column) domain configuration with monthly/daily and instantaneous history tapes
assumptions: All columns share identical location, climate forcing, and homogeneous loam texture so that differences in recharge arise solely from initial water-table depth.
The initial WTD is imposed as an initial condition (hydrostatic pressure profile above the water table); it is not encoded in the column soil_texture field.
The infiltration pulse is applied as an idealized rainfall/irrigation event; a ~2-week model spin-up precedes the pulse to establish drainage equilibrium at each WTD.
Deep unsaturated zone assumed to have the same hydraulic properties as the near-surface (no bedrock or aquitard) to keep the experiment idealized.
STOP_N=18 months provides enough post-pulse time for the wetting front to reach even the 50 m water table under loam properties; extend if recharge signal has not arrived.
Bare/low-vegetation or fixed-LAI configuration is used to minimize ET variability among columns.
Longitude given in 0-360 convention (261 = 99°W, U.S. central plains).
